title: EMP / Solar Storm
description: Use this list to get ready for a long, wide-area grid outage from a solar storm or a high-altitude EMP.

sources.title: Space weather: Storms from the Sun

items.text: Store water for at least 2 weeks (1 gallon / 3.8 L per person per day) and have a way to treat more - filter, bleach, or boiling
Store at least 2 weeks of shelf-stable food that needs no refrigeration; build toward a longer supply over time
Keep as large a reserve of daily prescriptions as your doctor and plan allow, and a written medicine list
Have a safe non-electric heat plan for cold weather (wood stove or vented heater) and battery CO alarms on every level
Never run a generator, grill, or camp stove indoors or in a garage - carbon monoxide kills more people in long outages than the event itself
Keep a spare battery or hand-crank radio (NOAA Weather Radio, or ham if licensed) stored in a closed metal container - test it before storing
Make a Faraday container: wrap spare electronics in 2-3 layers of heavy foil or anti-static bags, line a metal can or box with cardboard, and make sure the lid seals metal-to-metal all around
Store a spare power bank and small solar charger in the Faraday container
Store spare flashlights or headlamps and batteries in the Faraday container
Keep cash in small bills - ATMs, card readers, and banks may be down for a long time
Keep a well-stocked home first aid kit and take a first aid class - care may be hard to reach for weeks
Get to know your neighbors now - shared skills and supplies go further than one household's stockpile
Set up a sanitation plan for when toilets do not flush: bag-lined bucket with lid, extra bags, and disinfectant
Know how to fill containers with tap water right away when power fails, before pumps lose backup power
Keep paper copies of maps, phone numbers, account numbers, and important records
Keep basic hand tools for repairs and chores that do not need power (saw, hammer, pry bar, shovel)
Keep the car tank at least half full - most cars are expected to keep running, but fuel pumps need power
Make a household safety plan for a long outage: lock-up routine, who checks on whom, and a neighborhood watch
Store open-pollinated garden seeds in a cool, dark, dry place if you plan to grow food
Learn manual workarounds at home: garage door release, well or sump pump backup, and safe ways to cook
Skip marketing gimmicks like plug-in 'EMP shields' or stickers - unplugged gear in a sealed metal container is the proven basic
